To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AtNRT 2.5 is expressed in roots of Arabidopsis as a complex of 150 kD with AtNAR 2.1, and that it is the major contributor (63%) to cHATS.
AtNRT1.1 is the only transporter responsible for low-affinity nitrate uptake in Arabidopsis roots and that AtNRT3.1 is the main contributor to nitrate efflux.
the 150 kDA complex of AtNAR2-1 and AtNRT2-5 is the major transporter responsible for the constitutive high-affinitive nitrate uptake in Arabidopsis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a nitrate transporter complex that is responsible for the detection of low levels of nitrate and the subsequent initiation of the nitrate assimilation process.
the identification of a novel nitrate transport complex, which is the major component of cHATS and is responsible for the detection of low levels of nitrate.
the identification and characterization of a novel plasma membrane nitrate transport system in plants that is involved in the detection of nitrate and in the regulation of nitrate uptake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NRT2/NAR2 plasma membrane nitrate transporter complex represents the major component of cHATS in Arabidopsis roots.
AtNRT1.1 and AtNRT2s are the main nitrate transporters in Arabidopsis roots, and that they are responsible for the uptake of nitrate from the root environment.
AtNRT 2.5 is the major contributor in cHATS and the first to sense and respond to nitrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cHATS in A. thaliana is a constitutive, inducible, high-affinity nit rate transport system that is composed of a 150 KDa complex of AtNAR2 and AtNRT2.
the 150 kD complex of AtNAR2 and AtNRT2 is responsible for cHATS in Arabidopsis roots.

the NRT2 family of transporters in plants has evolved to respond to a wide range of nitrate concentrations in the root environment, with AtNRT2 family members being responsible for both the initial detection of nitrate in low concentrations and the subsequent induction of the major inducible nitrate transporters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 150 kD nitrate transporter complex of AtNAR2-1 and AtNRT2-5 is the major contributor of cHATS in Arabidopsis roots.
the 150 kD AtNRT2/NAR2 complex plays an essential role in the detection of nitrate and the subsequent initiation of the nitrate response.
AtNRT 2.5 is a major contributor to c HATS and is responsible for initial detection and uptake of trace amounts of nitrate in nitrate-starved plants.
